instruction.text: Emotions are often seen as being <t-green>positive</t-green> or <t-red>negative</t-red>. Drag the emotions to the fitting category.

feedback.finish: It can be easy to think you should always be happy and only feel positive emotions. However, negative emotions, or those that are less pleasant to experience, are also normal and important.

instruction.text: Emotions are often seen as being <t-green>positive</t-green> or <t-red>negative</t-red>. Drag the emotions to the fitting category.

feedback.finish: Emotions are never good or bad, but always helpful. They tell us more about ourselves and others. They give us information about how we feel and what we need.

instruction.text: Select the images to listen to the emotions and outcomes. Match the negatively perceived emotion with a more positive outcome.

feedback.finish: Negatively perceived emotions are often calls to action. They tell us that something is not quite right and that we should try to understand the problem and fix it. Here, the negative emotion was important for both boys to talk about how they feel and get the help they need.

a.sound: Charlie felt ashamed that he was falling behind in maths.

b.sound: He talked to his teacher and found the help he needed to catch up.

a.sound: Max feels guilty about skipping football practice.

b.sound: He told his parents he doesn’t want to play any more.
